 Lilly's Q3 EPS estimate collapsed from $10 to $7 in 30 days after three post-quarter acquisitions are expected to generate new charges. 
 Merck's Keytruda growth is set to moderate and a $250 million wholesaler timing benefit from Q3 2025 won't repeat this quarter. 
 Gilead's cash fell to $3.2 billion from $10.6 billion after three acquisitions, with an FDA decision on anito-cel due Dec. 23.

 Three big pharma names report third-quarter results on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. Merck ( NYSE:MRK ) opens with a 9 a.m. ET call. Eli Lilly ( NYSE:LLY ) follows at 10 a.m. ET, and Gilead Sciences ( NASDAQ:GILD ) reports after the close with a 4:30 p.m. ET webcast. 
 Consensus Estimates Heading Into Oct. 29 
 Acquisition charges distort the per-share comparisons for all three companies, so revenue provides the cleaner measure. Year-over-year figures compare with reported Q3 2025 and full-year 2025 results.

 Eli Lilly: Estimates Fell as GLP-1 Demand Climbed 
 Lilly trades at $1,281.91, up 18.7% year to date. Last quarter, revenue rose 47.7% to $22.97 billion, and EPS of $8.38 exceeded the $6.58 estimate. Mounjaro ($9.94 billion) and Zepbound ($4.93 billion) drove the gains. 
 LLY Earnings Explorer — 24/7 Wall St. The Q3 EPS consensus has fallen to $6.6684 from $9.9319 over the past 30 days. Lilly's guidance excludes acquired IPR&D incurred after June 30, and the company completed three infectious disease acquisitions after the quarter ended. Expect new charges.

 Also watch international Mounjaro uptake, the Foundayo ramp, and the retatrutide filing planned for Q1 2027. The CFO said future growth is "more driven by the penetration in the outside-the-U.S. market." The main risk is pricing, as U.S. prices fell 9% last quarter, excluding adjustments. 
 Story Continues Merck: Keytruda Faces a Tougher Comparison 
 Merck trades at $141.82, up 33.2% year to date but down 3.6% over the past week. Its partner is Moderna ( NASDAQ:MRNA ), and leaked cancer vaccine data with Moderna disappointed. Merck's second-quarter revenue rose 5.07% to $16.61 billion. Adjusted EPS of −$0.13 beat the −$0.26 estimate despite a $2.31 per share Terns charge. 
 The CFO warned that U.S. Keytruda growth "will moderate," and an approximately $250 million wholesaler timing benefit from Q3 2025 won't repeat. Watch the Keytruda QLEX ramp ($463 million last quarter), Winrevair ($588 million, up 75%), and the revenue outlook of $66.3 billion to $67.3 billion. 
 The key risk is exclusivity, which Keytruda loses in 2028, and the CEO has called that period "more of a hill than a cliff." 
 Gilead Sciences: HIV Strength Meets Two Launches 
 Gilead trades at $159.08, up 30.8% year to date. Second-quarter revenue rose 10.2% to $7.80 billion on HIV sales of $5.69 billion, up 12%. Management subsequently raised its 2026 product sales guidance to $30.1 billion–$30.4 billion. 
 Watch Yeztugo, which posted $232 million against a full-year target of about $1 billion. Also watch launch plans for BIC/LEN, as well as for anito-cel, which faces an FDA decision on Dec. 23, 2026. Income investors should keep an eye on the $0.82 quarterly dividend. 
 The key risk is a shrinking cash balance, which fell to $3.2 billion from $10.6 billion after the Arcellx, Tubulis, and Ouro deals. 
 Lilly Carries the Most at Stake Thursday 
 Lilly has the most to prove. Its shares have gained 56.3% over the past year, and the company is worth about $1.2 trillion. Even so, analysts made seven downward Q3 EPS revisions in the past 30 days and only three upward. Merck and Gilead mostly need steady execution. Lilly needs to show that international volume and new launches can outrun U.S. price erosion, and its 10 a.m. call will set the tone for the whole group.
